title: GATT Hierarchy Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js explorer of the follower robot's GATT tree: the RobotFollower device, the Robot Command Service, the WRITE-only Command characteristic, an optional READ and NOTIFY Status characteristic, and an example Battery Service. Students click boxes to see type, UUID, and properties, then act as the leader to read, write, subscribe, and look up UUIDs, with a message log that shows IRQ events and refusals.

educational.topic: BLE GATT services, characteristics, UUIDs, and properties
learningObjectives: Identify the device, services, and characteristics in a GATT tree
Identify the UUID that the leader uses to find the Command characteristic
Predict which operations (read, write, notify) a characteristic allows from its properties
Explain that data lives in characteristics, not in services or the device
prerequisites: GATT protocol, services, characteristics, and UUIDs from Chapter 12
Central and peripheral roles from Chapter 12

controls.label: Tree boxes
controls.purpose: Select the device, a service, or a characteristic

controls.label: Value text
controls.purpose: The value to write (editable for custom text)

controls.label: Write
controls.purpose: Leader writes the value to the selected characteristic

controls.label: Subscribe (notify)
controls.purpose: Leader subscribes to notifications, or unsubscribes

controls.label: Look up UUID
controls.purpose: Find an attribute by its UUID

simulation.modelType: Interactive data-model explorer with rule-based responses
assumptions: Command has only the WRITE property (_FLAG_WRITE = 0x0008), as in the Chapter 12 follower code
Status (READ and NOTIFY) and the Battery Service are extra examples not in the chapter code
Notifications arrive every 2 seconds and report OK when stopped or BUSY when the motors run
limitations: Attribute handles, descriptors, and service discovery are not shown

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Clickable tree with a detail panel and action buttons that succeed or explain the refusal
keyQuestions: Which box holds the value FORWARD?
Which UUID does the leader need to find the Command characteristic?
Why is Read refused on Command?
What would you change so the leader could read the last command?
commonMisconceptions: Every characteristic can be read and written
Any similar-looking UUID will find the characteristic
assessmentOpportunities: Labeling the five boxes before clicking
Prediction table for read, write, and subscribe
